**What now exists:** \\u0060PullRequestReviewDuplicateRule\\u0060 (Domain, the only place ids are ordered), \\u0060PullRequestReviewDuplicateConvergence\\u0060 (Daemon, the pass, a DI singleton shared by \\u0060AutoPrReviewEngine\\u0060 and \\u0060MessageSweepEngine\\u0060), and a claim-time refusal in \\u0060DispatchEngine.TryClaimAsync\\u0060. Tests use a new \\u0060ReplicatedFleet\\u0060 helper (two real stores of one owner exchanging events over the replication seam), reusable for any two-node behaviour.\\n- **Gotcha:** the pass reads every live auto-created pr-review task in the store, not one project\\u0027s. \\u0060PrReviewTaskEngineTests\\u0060 shares one database across tests, so tests there that sweep must use unique pull request references; two live tasks on \\u0060acme/widgets#42\\u0060 left behind by siblings would be converged.\\n- **Gotcha:** if both nodes run the pass before either abandon replicates, the twin\\u0027s stream gets two \\u0060TaskAbandoned\\u0060 events, one per node. That is harmless (the apply is idempotent) but the courier feed shows both. I accepted it rather than making the decision depend on which node originated the twin.\\n- **Left undone on purpose:** the mention-attach path in \\u0060AutoPrReviewEngine\\u0060 still attaches to the newest live task, so a mention can land on the twin first. I left it because the pass carries it to the survivor. The takeover sweep still does not terminate on Abandoned, and hold-layer task \\u00601cccd3f7\\u0060 is untouched.\\n- **Left undone:** the card still needs the root cause text, since I could not run board-mutating \\u0060h9k\\u0060
